channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Euro: ECB expectations support EUR against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report that the Euro (EUR) is little changed near the low 1.16s as markets await Thursday’s European Central Bank (ECB) meeting, where a 25 bps hike and a hawkish tone are anticipated.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Bulls struggle below the 100-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) pulls back on Tuesday after failing to hold its earlier advance. At the time of writing, the metal trades around $66 after reaching an intraday high near $67.19.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar retreats as Chinese imports fall short of expectations
item.description: NZD/USD declines 0.37% on Tuesday, trading around 0.5855 at the time of writing. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains under pressure following the release of mixed trade data from China, New Zealand’s largest trading partner.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Carry unwind boosts gains against US Dollar - DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes that the Japanese Yen (JPY) has become the best-performing US Dollar Index (DXY) currency in 2026, with USD/JPY falling below its end-2025 level of 156.70.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Loonie rally pauses before fresh gains - NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada's (NBC) Marion and Dahms highlight a strong Canadian Dollar (CAD) rally in Q3, driven by positive data and higher Oil and Gold prices, which pushed USD/CAD briefly below 1.38. They warn that new U.S. tariffs and trade uncertainty raise downside risks to Canadian growth.

item.title: Copper: Record prices and Chile supply issues – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Norman Liebke highlights that LME 3‑month Copper has set a new all‑time high above USD 14,530 per ton, supported by strong US demand and anticipated import tariffs.

item.title: Gold trader lower despite weaker US Dollar as Fed hike bets weigh
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains on the back foot during American trading hours on Tuesday, even as the US Dollar (USD) remains on the defensive. Rising Oil prices and expectations of a Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike weigh on the precious metal.

item.title: Brazilian Real: Election risks keep pressure on BRL against US Dollar – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities highlights that BRL faces elevated election-related risks, with USD/BRL having tested its 200-day SMA resistance over the past month. Drawing parallels with 2014, the bank sees risks skewed toward higher USD/BRL as markets remain concerned about Brazil’s fiscal outlook.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Strong jobs and CPI risks – BNY
item.description: BNY Markets strategist John Velis says a strong United States (US) jobs report has pushed expectations for a September Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike back above 60%, despite Governor Christopher Waller’s more cautious comments.

item.title: Euro holds steady as US Dollar struggles for traction
item.description: EUR/USD trades virtually flat near 1.1623 during American trading hours on Tuesday. The US Dollar (USD) struggles to hold its earlier gains, helping the Euro (EUR) recover from its intraday low.

item.title: European Central Bank: Clients see higher peak and later cuts – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Mark Wall and Michael Kirker report that survey respondents expect the European Central Bank (ECB) to continue hiking, with a strong bias toward another move in September and a terminal rate between 2.50% and 3.00%.

item.title: US Dollar: Crude rally and CPI risks shape path – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that Brent Oil’s surge toward $100 is pressuring stocks and bonds while giving the Dollar a modest lift. However, he stresses that Friday’s US August Consumer Price Index (CPI) will be decisive for the Federal Reserve’s September 16 meeting.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Tariffs boost role as funding currency – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities argues Canadian Dollar (CAD) is set to gain prominence as a global carry funding currency, with its carry/vol profile already comparable to Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Gold: Fed inflation focus and volatility risk – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Thu Lan Nguyen notes Gold has stabilised around USD 4,400 per ounce, with markets now focused on upcoming US inflation data as the key driver for the Federal Reserve’s September decision.

item.title: 155.00: Why the Japanese Yen just broke through the level that could define a new range
item.description: USD/JPY has suffered a sharp technical breakdown below the key 155.00 psychological threshold, extending losses toward 153.00 amid thin holiday liquidity, unwinding carry trade positions, and renewed political focus on Japan's monetary framework.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling faces fiscal and BoE risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses how United Kingdom (UK) Chancellor Healey’s pro-growth rhetoric and commitment to fiscal rules have left questions over funding, with EUR/GBP still range-bound.

item.title: Euro: Downside risks against US Dollar into ECB and Fed – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole notes that stronger second-quarter Eurozone growth and resilience to geopolitical and commodity shocks have kept the Euro (EUR) relatively expensive.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Oversold conditions help buyers regain ground
item.description: GBP/JPY rebounds on Tuesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) loses momentum following its sharp rise since the start of the month. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 208.90 after briefly falling to 207.10, its lowest level since December 2025.

item.title: Oil: Supply shocks lift price risks – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that energy risk dominates markets as Brent crude is expected to trade sustainably above $100, with Saudi facility disruptions and constrained Hormuz shipments tightening supply.

item.title: Canadian Dollar eases from highs as risk aversion buoys the US Dollar
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is giving back previous daily gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, as the risk-off mood amid escalating tensions in the Middle East offsets the positive impact of higher Crude prices on the commodity-sensitive Loonie.

item.title: Indian Rupee corrects sharply from two-month high as Oil price boils
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) retreats from its two-month high against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA inflation focus underpins carry – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes AUD/USD is holding above 0.7200 as Australian sentiment softens but inflation keeps the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) on alert.

item.title: Copper hits record highs amid US tariffs and supply concerns
item.description: Copper prices have accelerated their rally this week, reaching an all-time high of 14,697 per ton at the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Carry unwind supports gains against US Dollar - ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner argue that the recent Japanese Yen rally against the Dollar has been driven by optimistic expectations on Bank of Japan tightening and GPIF flows, amplified by thin US holiday liquidity.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Remains sticky to 20-day EMA
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is down 0.1% at around 1.1610 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Tuesday. The major currency pair trades lower as the US Dollar turns positive after a weak start.

item.title: Natural Gas: Risk premium sustained on Gulf disruptions – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Florence Schmit highlights that TTF Natural Gas remains supported by low European storage and disrupted Gulf LNG flows. The absence of meaningful U.S.-Iran progress keeps a structural risk premium in prices, with 2026 TTF seen averaging €60/MWh in Q4.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD dips below $4,400 as Middle East tensions grow
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) posts marginal gains for the third straight day on Tuesday amid risk-off sentiment as tensions in the Middle East escalate and Oil prices rally, strengthening the case for higher interest rates in the world's major economies.

item.title: British Pound: Seen weakening against Euro on hawkish BoE pricing – ING
item.description: ING strategist Francesco Pesole reports that Sterling gained modestly, helped by Chancellor John Healey’s first major speech stressing fiscal discipline and keeping long-end gilt moves aligned with global bond selling.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Momentum builds below 155 against US Dollar - MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Teppei Ino notes that USD/JPY has fallen below the bank’s 155 forecast floor, briefly trading under 154.50 and testing key Fibonacci retracement levels.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.88 per troy ounce, down 0.55% from the $66.24 it cost on Monday.
